answer: Neighborhood anchor scoring: each identity's reach is capped by the distinct, mutually non-adjacent clusters that route traffic to it, so a finished voyage across the graph must end at many independent hubs. An identity earns routing priority only when its inbound paths disperse rather than converge on one crystal of shared neighbors, and every new edge must attach to a differently anchored region. Cloning therefore costs the attacker a full set of scattered, non-overlapping connections per identity, priced at real latency and separate hosting per cluster.
